importantTopics: Divide and Conquer and Recurrence Relations
Dynamic Programming and Shortest Path Algorithms
likelyQuestions: Describe an O(n)-time method for merging two sorted arrays into a single sorted array containing unique elements.
Solve the 0/1 Knapsack problem using a branch and bound approach and illustrate it with an example.
Explain how Depth First Search (DFS) traversal can be utilized to find strongly connected components in a directed graph with an example.
Design an O(log n) time algorithm to find a specific element in an array that first strictly increases and then strictly decreases.
Use the Master Theorem to find the running times of given divide-and-conquer recurrences and justify the optimal algorithm choice.
Trace the Floyd-Warshall algorithm on a given weighted directed graph and show the distance matrices after each iteration.
Explain Huffman coding as a greedy approach for data compression, analyze its complexity, and construct an optimal prefix code for a given set of character frequencies.
Run the Bellman-Ford algorithm on a weighted directed graph to find single-source shortest paths, and explain how an extra iteration detects negative-weight cycles.
Explain the finite state automaton-based string matching algorithm and demonstrate its execution for a given pattern and text.
Define NP-complete problems and provide a formal polynomial-time reduction proof between two classical NP-complete problems such as Clique and Vertex Cover.
